editorial:
Imagine being the best shot in America and getting hired to travel halfway across the world just to shoot some wild dogs. That is exactly what happens to Matt Quigley. He lands in the Australian Outback thinking it is a simple job for a rich land baron named Marston. You will quickly see that Marston is actually a cruel man who wants to kill native people instead of dingoes. Once Quigley realizes he is being used for something evil, he refuses to help. This sets up a great game of cat and mouse across a beautiful, dusty landscape. Along the way, he meets Crazy Cora, a wild and funny woman who adds a lot of spark to the story.

What really makes this movie work is the balance between action and humor. Tom Selleck is perfect as the straight-man hero who just wants to do the right thing. The long-range shooting scenes are exciting and keep you on the edge of your seat. While the plot is a bit simple, it never feels boring. If you enjoy old-school adventures with a clear hero and villain, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge final showdown. Marston tries to kill Quigley, but Quigley uses his incredible skill with a long-range rifle to take him down from a distance. He proves that his honesty and talent are stronger than Marston's money and power. After the bad guy is gone, Quigley decides to stay in Australia. He settles down with Cora and the local people, finally finding a place where he truly belongs.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Westerns and adventure stories.
